title: ScreenSaverOverlay Z-order Fix on Visibility Show
desc: ScreenSaverOverlay Z-order fix: WPF Visibility.Hidden->Visible resets HWND Z-order; must re-apply topmost via Topmost-toggle + deferred SetWindowPos at DispatcherPriority.Loaded
steps: Root cause: WPF Window with Visibility=Hidden retains Topmost property but loses HWND Z-order. On Hidden->Visible transition WPF re-creates the window in default Z-order (just above desktop). A single SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST) immediately after Visibility.Visible runs before WPF finishes rendering so the Z-order change is lost.

Fix in ScreenSaverOverlay.Tick() wasHidden branch at csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI/ScreenSaverOverlay.cs around line 410: (1) set Visibility=Visible, (2) toggle Window.Topmost=false then true to force WPF to re-emit its internal SetWindowPos, (3) call native SetWindowPos(HWND_TOPMOST) immediately as the belt, (4) schedule deferred SetWindowPos at DispatcherPriority.Loaded as the suspenders -- runs after WPF rendering completes.

Why both immediate and deferred SetWindowPos: immediate covers fast paths, deferred covers WPF compositor races. The Topmost toggle is what triggers WPFs own internal SetWindowPos -- without it WPF thinks Topmost is already true and does nothing.
Verification: trigger screensaver via idle 10s+, confirm overlay appears in front of all visible windows (Chrome, file explorer, taskbar).

ROOT CAUSE (Win11 confirmed 2026-05-20): WS_EX_TRANSPARENT + WS_EX_TOPMOST combination causes Windows 11 to demote the window below regular non-topmost windows. Fix: remove WS_EX_TRANSPARENT from SourceInitialized exStyle, keep only WS_EX_NOACTIVATE+WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW+WS_EX_LAYERED. WS_EX_TRANSPARENT was used for click-through but GetUserIdleMs detects input without needing mouse interception so it is unnecessary.
